questions.stem: The fragmented red cells highlighted in this peripheral blood smear are specific for which process?

explanation.summary: These cells never appear in normal or artifactual smears; their presence indicates mechanical red-cell fragmentation from intravascular microthrombi, i.e., MAHA.
explanation.whyCorrect: These cells never appear in normal or artifactual smears; their presence indicates mechanical red-cell fragmentation from intravascular microthrombi, i.e., MAHA.

questions.stem: The labeled cells in this smear (including helmet cells and triangulocytes alongside intact red cells) point to which underlying pathology?

explanation.summary: Helmet cells and triangulocytes are morphologic subtypes of schistocytes, formed when red cells are cut passing through fibrin/platelet microthrombi in small vessels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Helmet cells and triangulocytes are morphologic subtypes of schistocytes, formed when red cells are cut passing through fibrin/platelet microthrombi in small vessels.

questions.stem: A patient with thrombotic microangiopathy has these skin findings. What is the most likely underlying cause?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased vascular fragility from vitamin C deficiency

explanation.summary: The petechiae and purpura pictured result from low platelet counts (consumed in microthrombi), which cause bleeding into the skin and oozing from small vessels.
explanation.whyCorrect: The petechiae and purpura pictured result from low platelet counts (consumed in microthrombi), which cause bleeding into the skin and oozing from small vessels.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the normal enzymatic cleavage of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers at the endothelium. Loss of this depicted function would most likely cause which disease?

explanation.summary: The enzyme shown normally cleaves ultra-large vWF multimers; its deficiency leaves these sticky multimers uncleaved, causing platelet-rich microthrombi characteristic of TTP.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enzyme shown normally cleaves ultra-large vWF multimers; its deficiency leaves these sticky multimers uncleaved, causing platelet-rich microthrombi characteristic of TTP.

questions.stem: The vessel depicted shows uncleaved ultra-large multimers trapping platelets into thrombi. As red cells are sheared passing these thrombi, which type of anemia develops?

explanation.summary: The platelet-vWF thrombi mechanically fragment passing erythrocytes, producing the microangiopathic hemolytic anemia seen in TTP.
explanation.whyCorrect: The platelet-vWF thrombi mechanically fragment passing erythrocytes, producing the microangiopathic hemolytic anemia seen in TTP.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a red cell contacting an intravascular thrombus and being cut as it passes. This mechanism is the basis of which finding in thrombotic microangiopathy?

explanation.summary: The thrombus acts like a blade, shearing intact erythrocytes into fragmented cells; this intravascular mechanical hemolysis defines microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thrombus acts like a blade, shearing intact erythrocytes into fragmented cells; this intravascular mechanical hemolysis defines microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
